questions.question: After you stop during the stop/start test, what should you do?

options.text: Do not use four-way flashers because this is a test, not an emergency.
Leave the bus in first gear.
Park in front of a fire hydrant.

questions.explanation: When you stop during the on-road test, turn on your four-way flashers and shift into neutral or park. Do not block driveways, intersections, fire hydrants, or signs.

questions.question: Where are the danger zones around a school bus?

options.text: Only in front of the bus.
Only in the back and on the left side.
In front, on the sides, and in the back.

questions.correctAnswerText: In front, on the sides, and in the back.
questions.explanation: Danger zones are areas where children can be hit by another vehicle or the bus itself. These areas are in front, on the sides, and in the back of the bus. Danger zones can extend 10 feet from every side of the bus.

questions.question: What is true about loading and unloading a school bus?

options.text: It can be dangerous for passengers.
It does not need to be watched or supervised.
It should be done while refueling the bus.
The driver can talk to other drivers while loading or unloading.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can be dangerous for passengers.
questions.explanation: More students are killed during loading and unloading than while riding the bus. Bus drivers must follow safety procedures and watch students carefully during loading and unloading.

questions.question: Why should a bus driver stop at least 10 feet away from waiting students?

options.text: Students walk to the bus, so the driver can see their movements better.
Students might get scared of the bus coming toward them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Students walk to the bus, so the driver can see their movements better.
questions.explanation: Stop the bus with the front bumper at least 10 feet away from waiting students. This makes students walk toward the bus, which lets the driver watch their movements carefully.

questions.question: If a tornado is approaching and there is no shelter nearby, where should students go?
questions.explanation: If you must evacuate the bus due to a tornado, lead students to a nearby building first. If no building is available, take them to a nearby ditch or culvert. Avoid areas with flood risk and stay far enough from the bus so it would not hit them if it tipped over.

questions.question: While students exit the bus, what should the driver watch for?

options.text: That students are leaving in pairs.
That students do not get caught on the handrail or door.
That students do not talk while exiting.
That students all have shoes on.

questions.correctAnswerText: That students do not get caught on the handrail or door.
questions.explanation: Watch students as they enter and exit to make sure they do not get caught in the door or on the handrails. Also make sure students move away from the bus after exiting.

questions.question: During the on-road driving test, you must do all of the following except:

options.text: Complete the test without any moving violations.
Obey traffic signs and signals only when other traffic is present.

questions.correctAnswerText: Obey traffic signs and signals only when other traffic is present.
questions.explanation: Drive safely during the on-road test. You must wear your safety belt, obey all traffic signs and signals at all times, obey all traffic laws, and complete the test without accidents or moving violations.

questions.question: If a tornado is approaching and the bus is evacuated, where should students go?
questions.explanation: If you must evacuate the bus because of a tornado, lead students to a nearby building first. If no building is available, take them to a nearby ditch or culvert. Avoid flood-prone areas and stay far enough from the bus so it would not hit them if it tipped over.

questions.question: What should be checked before operating a school bus?
questions.explanation: Check all mirrors before driving the bus. You need the maximum viewing area that meets Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standards. Have mirrors adjusted if needed.

questions.question: During the vehicle inspection test, you must do all of the following except:

options.text: Point to or touch each item.
Explain what you are checking and why.

questions.explanation: During the vehicle inspection test, walk around the bus, point to or touch each part, and explain what you are checking and why. You do not have to crawl under the hood or under the vehicle.

questions.question: When a school bus is approaching a bus stop, the driver should:
questions.explanation: School bus drivers must slow down and approach stops with care.

questions.question: If your bus stalls on a railroad track, what should you do?

options.text: Get everyone off the bus and move far away from it.
Keep everyone on the bus and try to stop the train by waving.
Keep everyone on the bus and wait for help.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get everyone off the bus and move far away from it.
questions.explanation: If a school bus stalls on railroad tracks, get everyone off the bus right away. Move away from the tracks at an angle, away from any coming train.

questions.question: Loading passengers onto a school bus:
questions.explanation: More students are hurt or killed during loading and unloading than while riding the bus. Drivers must follow safety rules carefully and supervise this process.

questions.question: During the driving test, the examiner will score you on:

options.text: How fast you reach your destination.

questions.explanation: The examiner will score you on your driving maneuvers and your overall driving behavior. You must drive safely, obey all traffic signs and signals, and avoid accidents or violations.

questions.question: During a basic vehicle control skills test, you may be asked to:

options.text: Drive forward into a parking space.

questions.explanation: Skills tests may include straight line backing, offset parking, parallel parking, and alley docking.

questions.question: For a basic vehicle control skills test, you should be able to:
questions.explanation: Skills tests may include straight line backing, offset parking, parallel parking, and alley docking.

questions.question: ABS helps you:

options.text: Keep your wheels from locking up.
Count the students boarding the bus.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your wheels from locking up.
questions.explanation: Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) stops your wheels from locking when you brake hard on a slippery surface.

questions.question: After students unload at school, the driver:

options.text: May assume students took all their belongings.
Should assume students cleared the doorway right away.
Should check the bus for sleeping or hiding students.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should check the bus for sleeping or hiding students.
questions.explanation: After students exit, the driver should walk through the bus to check for any students still inside, whether sleeping or hiding. Also check for items students left behind.

questions.question: The inside rearview mirror of a school bus is used to:

options.text: See in front of the bus.

questions.explanation: The inside rearview mirror is used to watch passenger activity inside the bus.

questions.question: A school bus must be evacuated if:

options.text: The bus stalls in winter weather.
There is any danger of a crash.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is any danger of a crash.
questions.explanation: Students should usually stay on the bus during emergencies. Evacuate if the bus is on railroad tracks, is on fire, or has a hazmat spill. Also evacuate if there is danger of a crash.
